title: Singapore-Cambridge O-Level
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public Singapore-Cambridge O-Level syllabus. Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: Read the sentence. The weary traveller trudged along the dusty road, his feet aching at every step. The word trudged most nearly means
items.explanation: Aching feet and a dusty road show slow, heavy walking, while running, resting and dancing all describe very different actions.

items.stem: Choose the word nearest in meaning to candid as used in the sentence. The headmaster gave a candid report on the state of the school.
items.explanation: Candid means honest and straightforward, so honest is the closest synonym, while confusing, lengthy and rude carry different meanings.

items.stem: Fill the gap with the correct verb. Neither the prefect nor the students ____ present when the bell rang.
items.explanation: With neither and nor the verb agrees with the nearer subject students, which is plural, so the correct form is were.

items.stem: Choose the word most nearly opposite in meaning to ancient in the sentence. The museum displays ancient pottery.
items.explanation: Ancient means very old, so its opposite is modern, whereas old and historic are close in meaning and famous is unrelated.

items.stem: Which of the following words has its primary stress on the second syllable?
items.explanation: Machine is stressed on the second syllable, maCHINE, while doctor, father and market all carry their stress on the first syllable.

items.stem: Which of the following words contains the long vowel sound heard in the word seat?
items.explanation: Seat contains the long vowel heard in see, while sit, bit and hit all contain the shorter vowel sound heard in sit.

items.stem: Choose the sentence that is correctly punctuated.
options: The boys, who arrived late missed the bus.
The boys who arrived, late missed the bus.
The boys who arrived late missed the bus.
The boys who arrived late, missed the bus.
items.explanation: The clause who arrived late is essential to identify the boys, so it takes no commas, unlike options that insert a comma in the wrong place.

items.stem: Choose the correct question tag to complete the sentence. The pupils have finished their homework, ____
items.explanation: A positive statement with the auxiliary have takes the negative tag have they not, matching the tense and person of the statement.

items.stem: Choose the word nearest in meaning to verbose as used in the sentence. His verbose speech lasted for over an hour.
items.explanation: Verbose means using more words than needed, so wordy is the nearest synonym, while brief is its opposite and silent and clear are unrelated.

items.stem: Fill the gap with the correct preposition. She has been living in Singapore ____ 2015.
items.explanation: Since is used with a point in time from which an action began, while for is used with a length of time such as five years.

items.stem: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence. If I ____ you, I would apologise at once.
items.explanation: The second conditional uses were for every subject, giving the standard subjunctive form if I were you, not am, was or be.

items.stem: Choose the word most nearly opposite in meaning to frugal in the sentence. The family lived a frugal life.
items.explanation: Frugal means economical or thrifty, so its opposite is extravagant, while thrifty and careful are close in meaning to frugal.

items.stem: Which of the following words contains a silent letter?
items.explanation: In comb the letter b is not pronounced and is therefore silent, while lamp, hand and tent have every letter sounded.

items.stem: Read the passage. Ada worked quietly all term and, when results were released, she had the best score although she never spoke about it. Which quality does Ada show?
items.explanation: She achieved the best score but did not boast, which shows humility, whereas pride, anger and laziness do not fit her quiet effort.

items.stem: Choose the correct form of the verb. The committee ____ its report before the meeting ended.
items.explanation: The committee acts as a single body here, so the singular past tense submitted is correct, while the other options do not agree or are ungrammatical.

items.stem: If 3x + 4 = 19, what is the value of x?
items.explanation: Subtracting 4 from both sides gives 3x = 15, so x = 5, and substituting back gives 15 + 4 = 19.

items.stem: Expand the product of the expressions (x + 5) and (x - 2).
items.explanation: Multiplying out gives x^2 - 2x + 5x - 10, which simplifies to x^2 + 3x - 10, matching only that option.

items.stem: Factorise the quadratic expression x^2 - 5x + 6 completely.
items.explanation: Two numbers that multiply to 6 and add to -5 are -2 and -3, so the factorised form is (x - 2)(x - 3).

items.stem: The first term of an arithmetic progression is 5 and the common difference is 3. What is the eighth term?
items.explanation: Using a plus seven d gives 5 plus 7 times 3, which equals 26, so the eighth term is 26.

items.stem: Find the simple interest on a principal of 5000 naira for 2 years at 10 percent per annum.
items.explanation: Simple interest is principal times rate times time divided by 100, giving 5000 times 10 times 2 divided by 100 which equals 1000.

items.stem: A right-angled triangle has legs of length 6 cm and 8 cm. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
items.explanation: By Pythagoras the hypotenuse squared is 6 squared plus 8 squared, which is 100, so the hypotenuse is 10 cm.

items.stem: Two angles lie on a straight line and one of them measures 65 degrees. What is the size of the other angle?
items.explanation: Angles on a straight line add up to 180 degrees, so the other angle is 180 minus 65 which equals 115 degrees.

items.stem: Simplify the product of 2 raised to the power 3 and 2 raised to the power 4, giving a single number.
items.explanation: Multiplying powers of the same base adds the indices, giving 2 raised to the power 7 which equals 128.

items.stem: Differentiate y = 4x^2 + 3x with respect to x.
items.explanation: Differentiating term by term gives 8x for 4x^2 and 3 for 3x, so dy by dx equals 8x + 3.

items.stem: Solve for x in the equation 2x - 7 = 3.
items.explanation: Adding 7 to both sides gives 2x = 10, so x = 5, and substituting back gives 10 minus 7 which is 3.

items.stem: Find the mean of the numbers 4, 8, 6, 10 and 12.
items.explanation: The sum is 40 and there are five numbers, so the mean is 40 divided by 5 which equals 8.

items.stem: What is the probability of obtaining a head when a fair coin is tossed once?
items.explanation: There is one favourable outcome out of two equally likely outcomes, so the probability of a head is 1/2.

items.stem: The area of a rectangle is 48 square centimetres and its length is 8 centimetres. What is its width?
items.explanation: Since area equals length times width, the width is 48 divided by 8 which equals 6 centimetres.

items.stem: If 5 raised to the power x equals 125, what is the value of x?
items.explanation: Since 5 multiplied by itself three times gives 125, the value of x is 3.

items.stem: Convert the decimal 0.75 to a fraction in its lowest terms.
items.explanation: The decimal 0.75 equals 75 over 100, which cancels down to 3 over 4 in its lowest terms.

items.stem: Which gas do green plants take in from the air during photosynthesis?
items.explanation: Plants take in carbon dioxide for photosynthesis and release oxygen, while nitrogen and hydrogen are not used in the process.

items.stem: What is the chemical symbol for the element sodium?
items.explanation: Sodium has the symbol Na, taken from its Latin name natrium, while S stands for sulphur and N stands for nitrogen.

items.stem: Which part of the human body pumps blood around the body?
items.explanation: The heart is a muscular pump that drives blood around the body, while the liver, lungs and kidney have other functions.

items.stem: Which of the following materials is a good conductor of electricity?
items.explanation: Copper contains free electrons and conducts electricity well, while rubber, plastic and dry wood are insulators.

items.stem: Which force pulls an object towards the centre of the earth?
items.explanation: Gravity is the force of attraction towards the centre of the earth, whereas friction, magnetism and tension act differently.

items.stem: Which of the following is the unit of electric current?
items.explanation: Electric current is measured in amperes, while the volt measures potential difference, the watt measures power and the ohm measures resistance.

items.stem: Which change of state occurs when a liquid becomes a gas?
items.explanation: Evaporation changes a liquid into a gas, while condensation is the reverse and freezing and melting involve solids.

items.stem: Which part of a plant cell carries out photosynthesis?
items.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll that traps light energy for photosynthesis, while the nucleus, cell wall and vacuole have other roles.

items.stem: Which of the following animals is a mammal?
items.explanation: The whale is a warm-blooded mammal that feeds its young on milk, while the lizard, frog and eagle are a reptile, an amphibian and a bird.

items.stem: Which acid is found in the human stomach and helps to digest food?
items.explanation: The stomach produces hydrochloric acid to aid digestion, while the other acids are found elsewhere or not in the body.

items.stem: What happens to the volume of a fixed mass of gas when it is heated at constant pressure?
items.explanation: At constant pressure a gas expands when heated, so its volume increases in line with the gas laws.

items.stem: Which of the following is a renewable source of energy?
items.explanation: Wind is renewed naturally and is inexhaustible, while coal, natural gas and petrol are finite fossil fuels.

items.stem: What is the main product formed when iron rusts in moist air?
items.explanation: Rusting is the reaction of iron with oxygen and water to form hydrated iron oxide, whereas the other compounds need different reactants.

items.stem: Which type of blood vessel carries blood away from the heart to the body?
items.explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, while veins and the vena cava return blood to the heart and capillaries link the two.

items.stem: Which of the following mixtures can be separated by filtration?
items.explanation: An insoluble solid such as sand can be filtered from water, while salt, sugar and alcohol dissolve and need distillation or evaporation.

items.stem: Which line of latitude divides the earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres?
items.explanation: The Equator at zero degrees latitude divides the earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres, while the tropics lie further north and south.

items.stem: What is the main cause of the day and night cycle on the earth?
options: Rotation of the earth on its axis
Revolution of the earth around the sun
Movement of the moon around the earth
items.explanation: The earth rotates on its axis once every twenty-four hours, so different sides face the sun and produce day and night.

items.stem: Which of the following is a primary source of historical information?
options: A documentary film made last year
An original letter written at the time
items.explanation: An original letter is a primary source created at the time of the event, while textbooks, encyclopedias and recent films are secondary sources.

items.stem: Which of the following is a feature of a democracy?
options: Permanent rule by a single party
items.explanation: Regular free and fair elections let citizens choose their leaders, which is central to democracy, unlike hereditary or military rule.

items.stem: What is the main function of the legislature in a modern state?
items.explanation: The legislature makes laws, while the judiciary interprets them and the executive carries out policy and commands the armed forces.

items.stem: Which of the following is a renewable natural resource?
items.explanation: Forests can regrow and be renewed if managed well, whereas crude oil, coal and tin ore are exhaustible mineral resources.

items.stem: The process by which water changes into vapour from the surface of the earth is called
items.explanation: Evaporation is the change of water into vapour, while condensation, precipitation and infiltration describe other stages of the water cycle.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes a constitution?
options: A list of ruling party members
A body of fundamental rules governing a state
A speech by the head of state
items.explanation: A constitution is the body of fundamental rules that governs a state and limits its powers, not a party list, speech or election record.

items.stem: Which of the following is an example of a civic responsibility of a citizen?
options: Paying taxes to a foreign country
Obeying the law and paying taxes
items.explanation: Obeying the law and paying taxes are duties a citizen owes to the state, whereas owning property or travelling are personal matters.

items.stem: What is the main reason for the apparent seasonal movement of the overhead sun between the tropics?
options: The tilt of the earth axis as it revolves
items.explanation: The tilt of the earth axis during its revolution makes the overhead sun shift between the tropics through the year.

items.stem: In a market economy, prices are mainly determined by
options: The forces of demand and supply
items.explanation: In a market economy the interaction of demand and supply sets prices, while decree, tradition or one producer would not be a market system.

items.stem: Which of the following was a major effect of the trans-Saharan trade on West African societies?
options: The growth of towns and the spread of Islam
The end of all farming activity
The removal of all existing trade routes
items.explanation: Trade across the Sahara linked West Africa to North Africa, encouraging the growth of towns and helping Islam to spread along the routes.

items.stem: Which document is regarded as the supreme law of a country?
items.explanation: The constitution is the supreme law to which all other laws must conform, while judgements, manifestos and ordinary acts rank below it.

items.stem: Which of the following is a physical feature of the earth surface?
items.explanation: A mountain range is a natural physical feature, whereas a capital city, a parliament and a factory are human-made features.

items.stem: The term population density refers to the
options: Total number of births in a year
Number of males in a country
Total land area of a country
Number of people living in a unit area
items.explanation: Population density measures how many people live in a unit area, usually per square kilometre, not births, males or total land area alone.
